metadata.description: Peak and off-peak pricing awareness for DeepSeek Harness: a live composer badge with the time left in the current window, converted to your timezone. Community plugin, not official.

paragraphs.text: Peak and off-peak pricing awareness for DeepSeek Harness: a live composer badge with the time left i
n the current window, converted to your timezone. Community plugin, not official.
**DeepSeek charges half price outside peak hours. This tells you when that is.**
COMMUNITY PLUGIN  ·  NOT OFFICIAL  ·  MIT  ·  DSH 0.2.x
Install  ·  Use  ·  How it works  ·  Timezones  ·  FAQ

> **This is a community plugin, not an official DeepSeek product.**
>
> Peak Hours is an independent

project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by,
> or supported by DeepSeek AI, and it is not part

of DeepSeek Harness. DeepSeek
> Harness and DeepSeek are names and marks of their respective owners.
## Why this exists

DeepSeek's API has two prices. Off-peak costs half of the peak rate. The windows
are written in UTC,
on a Beijing calendar, in a paragraph on the pricing page.

That is the correct way to define the policy and a terrible way to read it from
Tel Aviv at 17:35. Y

ou do the arithmetic in your head, guess, or notice the
difference on the invoice later.

Peak Hours puts one badge in the composer bar. It says **Peak** or **Off-peak**
and how long the cur

rent window has left. Click it and you get the day as a
clock face, the schedule in your own timezon

e, and the exact moment the price
changes.

The badge only appears while the session's selected model is served by DeepSeek
itself — the **DeepS

eek** and **DeepSeek Account** provider groups. A model
routed through another provider bills on tha

t provider's terms, so the plugin
never tells you it is off-peak on DeepSeek's schedule.
| | Peak | Off-peak |

| Rate | full price | **half price** |
| UTC | 01:00–04:00, 06:00–10:00 | every other hour |
| Beiji

ng | 09:00–12:00, 14:00–18:00 | nights, weekends, holidays |
| Days | Monday to Friday, not a Chines
e public holiday | weekends and holidays, all day |
The plugin answers one question: which column am I in, and for how much longer.
## What it looks like
Light and dark. The 24-hour face is your local day, with every peak window in amber and a marker for
and dark. The 24-hour face is your local day, with every peak window in amber and a marker for now.

The badge is small enough to ignore while you type. The ring drains over the
current window, so a gl
ance tells you whether you have minutes or hours.
| | Off-peak | Peak |

| Badge accent | green | amber |
| Ring | drains over the off-peak stretch | drains over the peak wi

ndow |
| Panel chip | half rate | peak rate |

loads lazily, so the badge appears after a reload.

No build permission is needed. The package ships plain JavaScript, has no

## How it works
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Three rules keep it honest:

1. **The policy is evaluated where it is written.** Peak windows are UTC
instants. Whether a day is

a peak day is a Beijing calendar question, so the
plugin asks the Beijing calendar, not your `Date`

object. A Friday 23:00 in
Los Angeles is a Saturday in Beijing, and the badge says so.
2. **The rend

ering is yours.** Those instants are formatted with `Intl` in your
own zone. Daylight saving time is

handled by the platform, not by fixed
offsets, and a 23 or 25 hour local day still draws correctly

on the face.
3. **No zone, no pretending.** If the runtime cannot resolve a timezone, the
plugin fal

ls back to Beijing time and labels the panel `Beijing time ·
fallback`. It never presents a guess as

g time and labels the panel `Beijing time ·
fallback`. It never presents a guess as your local time.

The badge is one registration in `conversation.input.right`. It reads the
composer's own model direc

tory — the same store the model selector renders
from, including the catalog default before a sessio

n has picked a model — and
renders only when that selection is a DeepSeek direct route
(`deepseek-of

ficial` or `deepseek-account`). A session that remembers a direct
selection still counts when the mo

del catalog cannot be read. It uses the
Harness theme tokens for every surface and text color, so it

follows your
theme, including custom ones. There is no Host route, no network request, and
no state

me, including custom ones. There is no Host route, no network request, and
no state written to disk.
## What it does not do

- It does not change what you pay or which model you use.
- It does not claim DeepSeek's window for

another provider: with a non-DeepSeek
model selected, the badge is absent.
- It cannot see where a D

eepSeek route points. If `deepseek-official` is
configured with a custom `baseURL`, the browser stil

l sees the DeepSeek
provider and the badge follows DeepSeek's published schedule.
- It does not call

the DeepSeek API, and it does not store your usage.
- It does not add a route, an event, or a backg

round process.
- It does not need a build step, a bundler, or a dependency.
## Compatibility

- DeepSeek Harness **0.2.x** (tested on `0.2.1-rc.1`, Desktop and Web).
- macOS, Windows, and Linux.

- Chromium 111 or newer, for `color-mix()` in the theme surfaces.
- One public slot: `conversation.

input.right`. Theme tokens only; no Harness
primitives, no monkey-patching, no DOM outside the compo

nent.
- Reads the composer's model directory (`modelDirectories`) and the session's
`modelSelection`

projection. If neither resolves a model, the badge stays
absent rather than guessing.

Developer preview means breaking changes. If a release moves the slot, the
plugin fails soft: the re

gistration disappears and the rest of the composer
keeps working.
